source_text.body:
Audit reproducibility of your published papers
A researcher used Claude to check the code and data of every journal paper they authored in the last five years and found significant reproducibility issues.
·
Nov 10, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
Mike Frank used Claude to audit the computational reproducibility of every journal paper he had co-authored in the last five years. The code and data for these papers were already publicly available, so the audit worked from those open materials. The post doesn't give the mechanics. They are in the linked blog post.
How it went
The audit found significant reproducibility issues, even though the papers' code and data were openly available. The post doesn't give counts or describe the specific problems.
Worth knowing
The papers' code and data had to be public for this audit to work. The post gives no cost or time figures, so check the linked blog post for those.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I have the code and data for my published papers in [folder path or repository links]. For each paper, try to set up the environment, run the analysis, and compare your results to the figures and tables reported in the paper at [path to paper PDFs]. Give me a report listing each paper as reproduced, partially reproduced, or failed, with the specific causes such as missing files, hardcoded paths, or unpinned dependencies. Do not modify my original files, and work in a copy.
Original source: https://bsky.app/profile/mcxfrank.bsky.social/post/3mzxtjeshsy2i
